exposure: Uterine artery embolization (UAE) during cesarean section
Two groups: UAE group and IABO group
Infrarenal aortic balloon occlusion (IABO) during cesarean section
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (birth weight, 1-min Apgar score, neonatal asphyxia rate, admission to Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, breastfeeding time)
Maternal recovery (duration of postpartum lochia, menstruation)
cohort: 62 patients with placenta previa combined with placenta accreta for planned cesarean section
finding: Infrarenal aortic balloon occlusion (IABO) was more effective than uterine artery embolization (UAE) in cesarean section of patients with placenta accreta spectrum, resulting in lower intraoperative blood loss, transfusion volume, radiation time, radiation dose, hysterectomy rate, duration of surgery, Intensive Care Unit admission, and complications.
birth_weight: Measured, but no specific findings reported
